title: P0 add artifact qualification and evidence activation interface contracts
description:
## Objective

Define measured-configuration evidence separately from bundle lifecycle. Add Python validators plus canonical and packaged schemas for LocalArtifactInventory, QualificationReport, and append-only EvidenceActivationRecord.

## Required evidence fields

QualificationReport includes report ID/digest, code-owned collector/issuer metadata, smoke/qualified/hold/failed status; exact immutable bundle-spec and artifact_set_digest; environment/qualification-workload/protocol fingerprints; fixed latency interval and result/mask-handoff IDs/versions; dataset/evaluation protocol, vocabulary ID, metric direction, and threshold context only when quality ran; UTC interval; `valid_until` no later than 90 days after completion; exactly three per-repeat aggregate summaries containing sample count, monotonic elapsed nanoseconds, p50/p95/p99, repeat throughput, whole-runner-tree RSS and accelerator-memory status; conservative cross-repeat aggregates; cold start; task-native quality only from predictions produced in the same run; resolved decoder/model-input/preprocess/postprocess identity; source/runtime provenance; and bounded limitations/failures. `image_e2e_validated_handoff_v1` starts immediately before decoding the pinned source bytes and ends only after preprocess, predict, postprocess, requested-class/prompt mapping, strict result and mask validation, mask encoding, and completion of the same bounded code-owned result/mask handoff used by execution. The final ManagedOutputTransaction directory rename/checksum publication is outside the interval. A different/partial interval is not comparable. Memory fields include exact collector ID/version/source, host process-tree or isolated cgroup/container scope, covered PIDs/devices without persistent device identifiers, collection interval, and known/unknown status. A known RSS value covers the maximum aggregate resident bytes of the complete runner process tree/group from runner creation through close; a known accelerator value covers memory attributed to all runner-tree processes on all declared devices for the same interval. Partial wrapper-only, leader-only, one-device, or unsupported backend measurements are unknown. It does not bind a mutable lifecycle projection. Do not store the 600 raw timing events. Representative-input performance evidence does not assert identical latency for every image-content distribution.

For a soft-real-time QualificationWorkloadProfile require a governed sustained-run section after cold start and warm-up. It resets the deterministic input schedule at index 0, starts a monotonic section clock immediately before that input's decode, and continues until at least 600,000,000,000 elapsed nanoseconds and the current strict validated handoff both complete. `processed_count` counts only successful complete handoffs; authoritative sustained throughput is the exact rational `processed_count * 1_000_000_000 / duration_ns`, compared without binary floating point. Retain every governed interval as one unsigned 64-bit nanosecond value in a preallocated at-most-8,000,000-byte array capped by fixed `max_sustained_samples=1_000_000`; p95/p99 use exact nearest-rank over all those samples. If the sample cap is reached before the duration/current-handoff condition, fail `sustained_sample_limit`; no reservoir sampling, approximation, overwrite, raw-event persistence, or silent early stop is allowed. Sustained memory covers the complete section and this array, and the report records queue/drop as not_applicable for this static sequential lane, known power/thermal observations, and termination/failure status. Warm-up, cold start, failed/partial results, and the three 200-iteration repeat samples are excluded from the sustained numerator and latency sample set. A failure or timeout invalidates the section rather than shortening it. For a batch profile omit it with explicit not_required reason. The 200-iteration repeats, their average, or an inference-only rate cannot make a soft-real-time bundle eligible. Do not decide after seeing results.

LocalArtifactInventory is produced by trusted preflight outside the pure selector and contains exactly one observation for every ordered artifact entry. Each observation records artifact_id/role/order, expected byte size/SHA-256, present/regular-file/type status, observed size/SHA-256 when readable, verification time, and bounded error status. `artifact_state_fingerprint` is canonical only over bundle spec/artifact_set_digest plus each artifact ID/order/status/observed size/hash; it excludes verification time, error text, and paths, so unchanged assets match on recheck. A separate full record digest includes the audit fields but is never pinned for execution. Every member must pass. The persisted form contains no absolute path. Registry/evidence cannot stand in for local presence.

EvidenceActivationRecord uses one stream per canonical selection key `SHA256(bundle spec, artifact_set, environment, qualification workload, protocol)`. Each event contains stream_id, monotonic sequence starting at 1, exact previous-event digest (zero sentinel only at sequence 1), report ID/digest, active/superseded/revoked state, activated/valid-until times, trust domain derived by the workflow, non-personal reviewer_role_id, bounded review-reference status, reason, and event digest. Project strictly by sequence, never timestamp; reject gaps/forks/duplicate sequence/wrong predecessor. At most one report is active for a key. Zero active is a valid projection only after a complete terminal revoke/withdrawal event and yields evidence_revoked/evidence_inactive abstention; it is invalid when an incomplete transition, dangling supersession, or history that still claims an active report caused the absence. A report ID/digest that becomes superseded or revoked can never become active again; revoked is terminal and corrected measurements require a new QualificationReport ID/digest. Conflicting active records or illegal reactivation fail validation/selection; the loader never chooses newest or best implicitly. Workspace-authored reports remain operator_asserted and non-selectable. The complete evidence_activation.jsonl control stream is capped at 8,192 records and 64 MiB before parsing/appending; exact-max is valid and one-over fails closed with `control_stream_limit_exceeded`. V1 has no automatic pruning, compaction, rollover, or second file. Capacity exhaustion requires a separate reviewed version/migration Bead with a new stream identity and compatibility plan; it never drops history or chooses a partial suffix.

Missing measurements are null with explicit status, never zero. Model-card quality/speed is catalog metadata, not qualification evidence. Checksums provide post-creation integrity, not issuer authentication; the local threat model trusts the repository-reviewed workflow and site operator, not an adversarial filesystem owner.

Use exact schema paths docs/schemas/local_artifact_inventory.schema.json, docs/schemas/qualification_report.schema.json, and docs/schemas/evidence_activation_record.schema.json, with same-basename packaged copies under yolozu/data/schemas. Update schema governance and discovery/browser tests.

For repository-managed public evidence, freeze `yolozu/data/adaptive_routing/qualification_reports/<report_id>.json` and the single append-only `yolozu/data/adaptive_routing/evidence_activation.jsonl` as source-controlled package data. `<report_id>` is a validated bounded ASCII identifier, never a path. site_managed reports/activation streams live only under an explicit site-confined evidence root supplied to local commands and are never copied into package/repository data. Projections are derived at load time; do not create a third index/projection file. The separate append-only public SupportProfileSpec SSOT is the bundle-lifecycle interface-contract path named above, never a caller workspace file.

## Non-goals

- No evidence loading/activation command, artifact hashing, model execution, selection, promotion, or copied public benchmark values.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Invalid/missing artifact-set members, unstable-state/full-record fingerprint confusion, activation gaps/forks, multiple active records per key, reactivation after superseded/revoked, future/expired evidence, personal actor fields, self-asserted managed trust, inconsistent repeat/sustained aggregates, different/partial latency intervals, phase-delay omission, warm-up/repeat contamination of sustained metrics, sustained-sample exact-max/one-over/early-cap/approximation cases, control-stream exact-max/one-over/partial-suffix cases, and contradictory artifact observations fail validation.
- Candidate-to-Experimental maturity/channel events do not stale a matching report; revoked/disabled/license-blocked lifecycle is rejected independently by selection.
- Qualified requires the normative repeat/performance fields; smoke cannot masquerade as qualified.
- Quality remains unknown when no matching evaluator/vocabulary ran; no raw images, filenames, absolute paths, private prompt/content hashes, or per-image timing events are retained.

## Verification

Add focused artifact/qualification/activation interface-contract tests, run schema-governance tests, and run git diff --check.

## Execution guardrails

- Inspect the referenced existing code and tests before editing; reuse them instead of creating a parallel implementation.
- Make the smallest additive change that satisfies this issue. Do not change public behavior outside this scope.
- Do not make a Stable support claim from fixtures, synthetic timing, public model-card numbers, or a successful import.

It emits UTF-8 with no BOM/whitespace; preserves array order; sorts object keys by their UTF-8 byte sequence; escapes quote, backslash, and U+0000..U+001F deterministically (short escapes for backspace/tab/LF/form-feed/CR, otherwise lowercase `\u00xx`); leaves other valid Unicode as UTF-8 without global normalization; and rejects duplicate keys, invalid Unicode/surrogates, NaN/infinity, binary floats, and booleans where integers are required. Integers use minimal base-10 with zero exactly `0`; fractional measured values in digested records use schema-bounded canonical decimal strings with no exponent, leading plus/zeros, trailing fractional zeros, or negative zero. Null/true/false are lowercase. A record's own digest field is omitted entirely while referenced predecessor/child/schema/artifact digests remain; SHA-256 is over these exact bytes and encoded lowercase hex. Pretty JSON is never hashed. Every language/path reuses this implementation and known ASCII/Unicode/key-order/decimal/own-digest vectors; do not use implementation-native object formatting or cite an unimplemented canonicalization standard.
- Every fractional threshold, metric, latency, FPS display, coordinate, and ranking value uses one `CanonicalDecimalV1` string. Its exact full-match grammar is `\A-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]{0,17})(?:\.[0-9]{0,8}[1-9])?\z` (or the target language's equivalent fullmatch), at most 18 integer digits, 9 fractional digits, and 29 bytes including sign/dot. Exponent, plus, leading integer zero, trailing fractional zero, bare dot, over-scale, and over-length tokens are invalid. A token whose exact numeric value is zero is valid only as `0`; reject `-0`, while negative nonzero values such as `-0.1` remain available only where that field permits negatives. Each field schema further fixes sign and numeric range. Parse to an exact signed integer coefficient plus scale and compare/order/gate using checked arbitrary-precision integer scale alignment or an exact Decimal context with traps and no rounding. Never compare strings, convert to binary float, or use locale. Known vectors include valid `0`, `0.1`, `0.000000001`, `1.1`, and permitted `-0.1`; numeric 2 versus 10 and -2 versus -10; rejected equivalent/noncanonical spellings; 9-digit scale max/one-over; huge-token rejection; and exact just-at/over gates. Schemas, qualifier aggregation, selector ranking, reports, and decision traces reuse this implementation.
- Use authoritative units and names across every adaptive-routing schema. Request/report/decision latency and cold-start values are nonnegative CanonicalDecimalV1 milliseconds named `*_latency_ms` or `*_cold_start_ms`; do not store unlabeled p50/p95/p99 numbers. Monotonic measured intervals and elapsed durations are unsigned integer nanoseconds named `*_duration_ns`; memory and byte sizes are unsigned integers named `*_bytes`; counts are unsigned integers. Throughput/FPS gating is authoritative from an integer processed/sample count and integer duration_ns exact ratio; an optional CanonicalDecimalV1 display is rounded only for display by a fixed documented rule and is excluded from digests, comparisons, and gates. Unit-mismatch, second-versus-millisecond, float, overflow, display/gate divergence, and missing-unit fixtures must fail.
- Every persisted UTC instant uses exact RFC3339 UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`: four-digit year, valid Gregorian calendar date, two-digit fields, no offset, fractional second, leap second, or alternate spelling. title: P0 add immutable algorithm bundle and lifecycle interface contracts
description:
## Objective

Define exactly what can be routed. Add Python validators plus canonical and packaged schemas for immutable AlgorithmBundleSpec, AlgorithmBundleRegistry, and append-only BundleLifecycleRecord.

## Required bundle fields

AlgorithmBundleSpec contains only immutable facts: bundle family_id, bundle ID/version and spec digest; provenance_class=`existing_code_owned|screened_candidate`; for a screened candidate, exact screening stream key plus onboarding pass-record ID/digest and source revision; test_only; tasks/prompt modes; allowlisted runner ID/version; execution_trust_class=`code_owned_audited|third_party_isolated`; required loader/serialization format and unsafe_deserialization_required flag; model/source immutable revision; runtime/provider, precision, architecture, accelerator/memory requirements; model input shapes; decoder/preprocess/postprocess identities; execution_network_required; and typed runner options. `bundle_version` is an exact 1..64-byte ASCII token matching `[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._-]{0,63}`. It is never normalized or parsed as SemVer; deterministic comparison uses the validated UTF-8 bytes, so `1.0`, `1.00`, `1.0-rc1`, and `1.0-rc01` remain distinct exact strings. family_id is a bounded immutable canonical identifier shared only by substitutable versions of the same pipeline semantics; changing task/output/vocabulary family requires a new family_id. code_owned_audited means the adapter is repository-owned/reviewed and uses only an already shipped, version-pinned, approved runtime/provider in the host TCB. A bundle-supplied executable/plugin/code/archive/setup hook, unsafe weight deserialization, or unknown classification requires third_party_isolated plus an immutable execution-isolation policy/backend digest; it can never import/load on the host. Do not classify the already shipped PyTorch/ONNX Runtime/TensorRT provider itself as bundle-supplied merely because upstream is third-party. Forbid arbitrary commands, Python module paths, environment assignments, and free-form argument arrays.

Represent every runner-consumed model/pipeline asset as an ordered `artifacts` list of 1..32 required entries plus canonical artifact_set_digest. Each entry has unique artifact_id, order, role (`code_archive`, `weight`, `config`, `class_vocabulary`, `tokenizer`, `engine`, or `auxiliary`), immutable source/revision, mandatory expected byte size 1..17,179,869,184 (16 GiB), SHA-256, immutable license identity/expression and license source, and an immutable logical cache_key. artifact_id is one 1..128-byte ASCII component matching `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}`, is neither `.` nor `..`, and is unique after exact ASCII comparison; slash, backslash, Unicode lookalikes, and normalization collisions are invalid anywhere an ID becomes a filename. Do not put approval/review state in the spec. cache_key is 1..8 slash-separated ASCII components, at most 512 bytes total; each component follows the same component grammar and is neither `.` nor `..`. It is not an arbitrary/absolute filesystem path. The prepared-candidate key `prepared_candidates/<candidate_id>/<build_id>/artifacts/<artifact_id>` is therefore valid and is the same governed asset, not a second copied file. The summed expected size must be at most 68,719,476,736 bytes (64 GiB). There is no optional runner-consumed asset in v1: changing which asset is present changes the immutable bundle/artifact set and requires new qualification. Composite Grounding-DINO/SAM and OCR detector/recognizer pipelines never collapse to one hash. Preflight checks regular-file stat size against the per-member and total caps before reading or hashing.

Define a code-owned ArtifactResolver shared by recommend, qualify, and process. It opens exactly one store root: the existing default `~/.cache/yolozu/models`, or one explicit artifact_root that must resolve inside the declared workspace. Resolve cache_key component-by-component relative to the already opened root with no-follow semantics; reject symlinks, escapes, non-regular files, ownership/type changes, duplicate resolved files, and roots/keys supplied by registry runner options. Paths and root identity remain local. A sensitive local-only artifact_resolver_state_digest binds resolver version, store kind, root identity, and ordered cache keys between recommendation and execution; it may appear only in the returned decision/user-owned provenance, never evidence/logs/public exports.

For fixed_classes, require an immutable class-vocabulary ID/digest and the ordered 1..10,000 NFKC-normalized canonical labels inline in AlgorithmBundleSpec under the 4-MiB spec cap. A class_vocabulary artifact may duplicate that governed source, but the pure selector never opens it or obtains labels from LocalArtifactInventory. Reject duplicate normalized labels. The selector may map a request only by exact normalized subset membership and returns both request-index to bundle-class-index and inverse retained-class mappings; core code never guesses synonyms, translations, or fuzzy matches. The immutable postprocess filters out every native detection whose bundle class is not requested, maps each retained native class to the pinned request index and normalized requested label, and rejects any non-integral/out-of-range/unmappable native class before output.

Text-prompt bundles explicitly declare dynamic_text and their actual prompt support. Their typed runner output identifies a class only by an integral zero-based request-prompt index. The adapter may resolve token spans internally, but core ignores/rejects model-generated label strings, maps the validated index only to the exact pinned normalized requested phrase, and rejects negative/non-integral/out-of-range/unmappable indices. Fixed-class and text mappings are part of the postprocess identity and local job/decision binding. Qualification and execution must use the identical mapping and adversarial-label handling.

Do not put enabled/disabled/revoked, maturity, human approval, or channel pointers in the immutable spec. BundleLifecycleRecord uses one global stream_id `bundle-lifecycle-v1`, monotonic sequence starting at 1, exact previous-event digest (zero sentinel only for sequence 1), event scope/type, non-personal reviewer_role_id, bounded public review reference or site-local reference status, issuer claim, source trust domain, reason, UTC time, and event digest. It is a strict discriminated union: `bundle_global` records require family_id, concrete bundle-spec/artifact-set digests and a complete artifact_id-to-license-review map with exactly `approved|unknown|blocked` for every artifact; concrete `channel_assignment` records require family/channel plus target spec and the support/evidence fields defined below; `channel_none` records require family/channel and prior-pointer audit fields but forbid a target spec and target artifact-review map. Unknown/blocked is valid global lifecycle history but ineligible for activation/selection/promotion. `bundle_global` disable/revoke/license-block applies to that bundle spec and artifact set in every channel; `channel_assignment` promotion/rollback changes only one named `(family_id, Candidate|Experimental|Stable)` pointer and never globally revokes the spec. Define each channel key's current pointer as a registered same-family bundle spec digest or immutable `none`. Eligibility-at-append applies only to a public Experimental/Stable concrete assignment or rollback target. `candidate_registration` requires a registered same-family structurally valid spec, provenance/screening binding where applicable, and a complete artifact-review map that may honestly contain unknown/blocked; it remains nonselectable and needs no qualification. A later global disable/revoke/license block may make a still-pointed public spec ineligible before rollback. Initial registration appends the nonselectable Candidate pointer using the explicit empty-profile variant below. A bundle spec may be pointed to by more than one channel; a global revocation excludes it from all of them, while a rollback of one channel leaves the other pointer unchanged. `bundle_global revoked` is terminal for that exact spec/artifact set and no later event may un-revoke it; remediation requires a new immutable version/spec. A reviewed enable may reverse disabled only, and a reviewed approved license event may replace unknown/blocked only without rewriting history. Project strictly by sequence, never timestamp; reject gaps, forks, duplicate sequence, wrong predecessor, family/artifact mismatch, missing/extra review-map entries, contradictory union fields, illegal un-revoke, or multiple assignments to one key at one sequence. Promotion/revocation/license review appends records and never edits an old spec/event. A JSON field cannot self-assert `yolozu_managed`: the loader derives trust from the governed source path.

Define immutable SupportProfileSpec for public packaged channel scope: bounded profile ID/digest, task, exact measured EnvironmentProfile fingerprint, exact QualificationWorkloadProfile and protocol fingerprints, every advertised SLO/quality constraint, and public limitations; it contains no user/site/private values. V1 does not extrapolate one evidence record across an undefined hardware class; a broader equivalence set requires a later separately measured interface contract. Store at most 128 definitions and set assignments in one canonical global append-only `SupportProfileRecord` chain at `yolozu/data/adaptive_routing/support_profiles.jsonl`. Each bounded record has kind=`profile_definition|profile_set_assignment`, stream ID `support-profiles-v1`, monotonic sequence, exact previous-record digest, and record digest computed with its own digest field omitted. The projected `support_profile_index_head` is the last validated record digest; it is not stored inside that same record. A set assignment names one `(family_id, Candidate|Experimental|Stable)` key and a complete ordered 1..32 dormant reviewed profile ID/digest set plus canonical set digest; an absent assignment means no reviewed set, and an empty set-assignment record is invalid. Its profiles must already have unchanged definitions in the same validated chain. Existing records are never edited/removed, and projection is by sequence, not timestamp. The support-profile set is the reviewed scope eligible for a future assignment; the active advertised scope is uniquely the snapshot in the current BundleLifecycleRecord channel assignment. A lifecycle target none therefore advertises empty without rewriting the dormant reviewed set.

A channel-assignment lifecycle record contains support-profile references according to its variant. `candidate_registration` targets a concrete Candidate spec but is nonselectable and requires an empty new profile set, no evidence bindings, `support_profile_index_head` equal to the zero sentinel when the chain is empty or the exact current head when present, `profile_set_record_id/digest=none`, and the shared canonical empty-set digest. It does not depend on the later support-profile implementation. `public_assignment` to a concrete Experimental/Stable spec requires the exact current index head and dormant-set record/digest, 1..32 profiles, and exactly one current evidence-activation ID/digest/trust-domain per profile; every activation selection key must exactly match that profile's bundle/artifact-set/environment/workload/protocol fingerprints and public packaged assignment accepts only yolozu_managed evidence. `channel_none` has no target bundle-spec/artifact review map, requires an empty new set and no target-evidence bindings, and instead audit-binds the exact prior pointer/spec/artifact-set digest or prior none plus prior active lifecycle snapshot's historical support-profile index head, set-record digest, and prior set digest; global artifact review remains in separate bundle_global events. A later reviewed dormant-set change never changes that prior active snapshot. Reject a target-spec requirement for none, missing target fields for concrete assignments, duplicate/missing/extra profiles, unknown/stale index heads or set-record heads, profile changes, environment/workload/protocol mismatches, mismatched evidence selection keys, non-current evidence, and caller subsets. Initial baseline/candidate registration fixtures prove both an empty-chain zero sentinel and a later nonempty-head/none-set registration are valid without qualification; only later Experimental/Stable public assignment activates an advertised set.

Use exact schema paths docs/schemas/algorithm_bundle_spec.schema.json, docs/schemas/algorithm_bundle_registry.schema.json, docs/schemas/bundle_lifecycle_record.schema.json, docs/schemas/support_profile_spec.schema.json, and docs/schemas/support_profile_record.schema.json, with same-basename byte-equivalent packaged copies under yolozu/data/schemas. Update docs/schema_governance.md and schema discovery/browser tests. Each fact distinguishes known presence/absence from unsupported or failed probing.

Validators must reject unknown keys, future schema versions, booleans used as numbers, NaN, infinity, negative limits, invalid hashes, unbounded prompt/input data, and unsupported enums. Canonical serialization must use allow_nan=False. Environment fingerprints exclude collection time, errors, paths, raw output, usernames, hostnames, serials, UUIDs, and IPs but include performance-relevant known hardware/runtime and power/performance-mode values.

Changing only prompt words within the same performance bucket changes local_job_digest but not this fingerprint. Tests reject cross-mode throughput fields, memory_first+auto, accuracy_first without the complete quality identity, contradictory compute/provider restrictions, non-finite quality thresholds, invalid direction, and absent/mismatched evaluation dataset/vocabulary/protocol.

title: P0 define adaptive image routing v1 policy
description:
## Objective

Write the normative v1 policy that later schemas, selector code, MCP tools, and tests must follow. Create docs/adaptive_image_routing.md and update docs/production_readiness.md only where needed to register the new Experimental lane.

## Rationale

The current repository can diagnose parts of the environment and benchmark selected paths, but it has no governed meaning of recommended, exact evidence-matching rule, or deterministic abstention policy. Freezing these decisions first prevents later tasks from inventing incompatible ranking, privacy, and qualification semantics.

## Alternatives Considered

- Choose a universal best model: rejected because task, host, runtime, license, and workload evidence varies.
- Add a weighted balanced score first: rejected because undocumented weights can hide hard tradeoffs and change when candidates change.
- Let the AI client choose a backend directly: retained only as an explicit manual path; it is not evidence-based routing.
- Defer policy until model adapters exist: rejected because adapters would otherwise define conflicting interface contracts and claims.

## Required decisions

- Supported tasks: object_detection and instance_segmentation.
- Supported inputs: single_image and bounded_directory. Define one explicit maximum image count; do not leave it unbounded.
- P0 batch size and concurrency are both 1. `execution_mode` is exactly `batch` or `soft_realtime`; it is not inferred from an FPS field.
- Prompt modes: fixed_classes and text. Missing qualified text support causes abstention. Define the bounded normalized prompt payload and make clear that the AI client compiles free-form instructions into short object phrases. A fixed-class request must be an exact normalized subset of the bundle's immutable class vocabulary; the core never guesses synonyms or translations.
- Selectable maturity: Stable or explicitly allowed Experimental; never Research.
- Execution network policy: audited code-owned runners declare and implement no network use. This is an application-level execution policy in P0, not OS-enforced isolation; enforced candidate isolation is defined separately in P1.
- For yolozu_managed/public selection, a channel is eligible only when the exact environment/workload/protocol and advertised gate semantics match exactly one SupportProfileSpec in that channel's current lifecycle snapshot; otherwise support_profile_mismatch. site_managed evidence may select outside that public set only with support_scope=site_qualified and never creates a public claim. Evaluate this per channel first. If the identical spec_digest is then eligible/current in more than one allowed channel, collapse it to one CandidateEvaluation and choose effective_channel by fixed priority Stable before Experimental among matching channels; record all pointed and matching channels in the bounded trace. Candidate is not selectable. Different spec digests remain distinct.
- Fix the lexicographic orders, after all hard filters, as follows. Every quality key is direction-aware: descending only for higher_is_better and ascending for lower_is_better, after exact metric, direction, dataset, protocol, and evaluation-vocabulary match. `accuracy_first` requires the complete quality requirement in ImageJobSpec and ranks matching task-native quality by its direction, p95 ascending, peak RSS ascending, then the canonical identity tuple `(family_id, bundle_id, exact bundle_version UTF-8 bytes, spec_digest)` ascending; missing/unknown/mismatched quality rejects validation or the candidate. For every other policy, if the job supplies a complete quality object, all surviving candidates must match that exact comparability key, the threshold remains a hard gate, and the direction-aware measured value is used at the stated quality tie-break. If the job omits quality, omit the quality key entirely for every candidate; never compare candidate-native metrics/datasets or prefer merely-known quality. `latency_first`: p95 ascending, optional job-defined quality tie-break, peak RSS ascending, then the identity tuple; p95 unknown excludes. `throughput_first`: sustained FPS descending for soft_realtime or repeat throughput descending for batch, then p95 ascending, optional job-defined quality tie-break, then the identity tuple; the chosen throughput metric unknown excludes. `memory_first` is invalid with compute_policy=auto. With accelerator_required it ranks known peak accelerator memory, then peak RSS, p95, optional job-defined quality tie-break, then the identity tuple. With cpu_only accelerator memory is not_applicable and it ranks peak RSS, p95, optional job-defined quality tie-break, then the identity tuple. Unknown applicable memory never becomes zero. Do not add a vague balanced score in v1.
- Unknown values never satisfy hard constraints. Abstained is a valid routing outcome, not an internal error.
- Bind measured evidence to immutable bundle spec plus ordered artifact-set digest, privacy-safe environment, qualification workload, and protocol fingerprints. Validate the current lifecycle projection independently: revoked, disabled, or license-blocked excludes selection, while a maturity/channel-only event does not stale the measurement collected while Candidate. SelectionDecision pins the current lifecycle digest only for recommendation-to-execution tamper detection. State that the environment fingerprint identifies a measured configuration, not a unique physical host.
- Keep three identities separate. A sensitive local-only job digest binds the actual normalized prompt/request between recommendation and execution. A sensitive local-only input digest binds the ordered input bytes without exposing filenames. The shareable QualificationWorkload fingerprint contains only decoded/performance characteristics and prompt mode/count plus maximum-codepoint buckets 1-16/17-32/33-64/65-128/129-256 and total-UTF-8-byte buckets 1-256/257-1024/1025-2048/2049-4096, never prompt text or either sensitive digest. For an accuracy gate, require an exact approved evaluation-vocabulary/protocol ID; an unseen/private vocabulary without matching local evidence causes abstention.
- Define input safety constants for v1: max_images 1..100; decoder allowlist JPEG, PNG, and single-frame WebP; source file at most 64 MiB; source total at most 512 MiB; width/height at most 16,384; decoded pixels at most 64 million per image and 512 million total. Reject archives, animation, malformed/decompression-bomb inputs, and symlink escapes before model load.
- Define output safety constants: max_results_per_image 1..1,000, at most 1,000 mask artifacts, at most 1,003 output files including the three required JSON files, and at most 4 GiB total output. A deployment may choose smaller declared limits; it may not exceed these v1 caps.
- Cap a registry at 128 bundle specs and 4,096 lifecycle events, and one recommendation input at 512 evidence reports, 4 MiB per control/evidence JSON record, and 128 MiB total. Before object construction, every file-backed control, registry, lifecycle, screening, build, evidence, or decision JSON record uses one shared bounded token parser: UTF-8 only, no duplicate object keys, depth at most 64, at most 100,000 aggregate object members plus array items, key length at most 256 UTF-8 bytes, and individual string length at most 1 MiB. Reject malformed, over-depth, over-node, over-key, or over-string input before allocating the full object; a byte cap alone is insufficient. Large user-owned predictions/stream/tracking/OCR result sets are not control records and use separate incremental writers/validators under their own row/text/file/byte caps; they are never loaded as one unrestricted DOM.
- SelectionDecision lists every validated candidate and exclusion; it is never silently truncated. CandidateEvaluation contains only bounded IDs/digests, rank state, at most 32 enum reason codes, at most one 256-UTF-8-byte detail per reason, a 1,024-byte human summary, and at most 32 bounded ranking-trace steps. The complete canonical SelectionDecision is at most 1 MiB. If all validated candidates cannot fit without omission, fail `registry/evidence_limit_exceeded` before choosing a winner.
- Reuse the current benchmark default of 20 warm-up iterations and 200 timed iterations per repeat; require exactly three completed repeats and nearest-rank p50, p95, and p99 using sorted index `ceil(p*N)-1`. Define cold start as wall-clock time from creation of a fresh runner process/sandbox before probe/load/deserialization through the first strict validated postprocessed result for input index 0, with no reused runner/model state; record OS cache state as uncontrolled rather than claiming a cold filesystem cache. Timeout/failure is not a numeric pass. Bind this definition, schedule, and memory collector ID/version/source to the protocol ID. `runner_tree_peak_rss_bytes` covers the whole fresh runner process group/tree from creation through close, never only the wrapper/leader PID; for an isolated runner use the live backend cgroup/container peak that covers every member. `accelerator_process_tree_peak_bytes` covers device memory attributed by the vendor/backend API to every runner-tree process on every declared device during the same interval. A collector that cannot prove full-tree/cgroup or full-device coverage returns unknown, never a partial number, and memory comparability requires the same collector identity/scope. For batch, every latency/memory gate and ranking key uses the conservative cross-repeat values: minimum repeat throughput and maximum p50/p95/p99/RSS/accelerator memory. Call this repeat throughput, not sustained FPS. Shorter runs are smoke evidence only. For soft_realtime, every throughput/latency/memory/drop gate and ranking key uses only the separate minimum ten-minute sustained-section aggregates; the 200-iteration fields are diagnostic and cannot satisfy those gates.
- Define evidence activation and freshness: exactly one active evidence ID per immutable bundle/artifact-set/environment/qualification-workload/protocol selection key; QualificationReport validity ends no later than 90 days after collection; report supersession or any immutable bundle/artifact-set/runtime/environment/workload/protocol mismatch invalidates it earlier; future-dated evidence is invalid. Revoked/disabled/license-blocked current lifecycle excludes execution without rewriting the report; maturity/channel-only events preserve measurement validity. Multiple active records for one key cause evidence_conflict and abstention rather than cherry-picking.
- Define trust domains `yolozu_managed`, `site_managed`, `operator_asserted`, and `unknown`. Checksums detect mutation but do not authenticate a claim. Workspace custom registries/reports begin as operator assertions; a report produced by the code-owned qualifier can become site_managed only through explicit local review/activation and can support only `site_qualified`, never a YOLOZU Stable/public claim. yolozu_managed requires a canonical bundle, public/non-sensitive inputs and protocol, a repository-owned reproducible qualification artifact, and explicit repository review/activation; trust is derived from that workflow, not a JSON field. Unknown/operator-asserted issuer status abstains by default.
- Define every exported `actor`, `owner`, or reviewer as a bounded non-personal role ID such as site_operator, repo_maintainer, release_reviewer, or automation. Never derive it from git username/email or a support account. Identifying consent/review references stay site-local; exported consent contains only status, scope, and date, and public review references are bounded repository-owned IDs.
- Define soft real-time as an SLO measured for one environment/workload/protocol fingerprint. Hard real-time is unsupported.
- Define catalog recommendation versus site-qualified recommendation and forbid universal best claims.
- Include selected and abstained examples plus stable machine-readable reason codes.

## Non-goals

- No Python implementation, schema, model integration, or benchmark run.
- Do not claim any current algorithm meets an SLO.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The policy resolves every required decision without TBD, appropriate, best available, or equivalent placeholders.
- It separates confirmed absence from probe failure and public benchmark evidence from site evidence. It also states that representative-image timing does not prove latency for every possible image-content distribution.
- It forbids retaining raw images/prompts, image/prediction/private-dataset content hashes, usernames, hostnames, IP addresses, device serials, and raw timing events in exported evidence, telemetry, logs, or public summaries. Sensitive aggregate job/input digests may exist only in the MCP-returned decision and user-owned local provenance to detect prompt/input replacement; per-file hashes are never persisted. Workspace-relative input/mask identifiers may exist only inside user-declared local output required by the existing interface contract.
- The maturity wording matches existing production-readiness documentation.

## Verification

Run python3 -m unittest tests.test_research_lane_docs tests.test_manifest_docs_references and git diff --check.

## Execution guardrails

- Inspect the referenced existing code and tests before editing; reuse them instead of creating a parallel implementation.
- Make the smallest additive change that satisfies this issue. Do not change public behavior outside this scope.
- Do not make a Stable support claim from fixtures, synthetic timing, public model-card numbers, or a successful import.
- Missing optional dependencies or target hardware must produce an explicit skip, hold, abstention, or blocked state; do not fabricate a successful path.
- Every adaptive-routing digest reuses one code-owned `canonical_json_v1` implementation. It emits UTF-8 with no BOM/whitespace; preserves array order; sorts object keys by their UTF-8 byte sequence; escapes quote, backslash, and U+0000..U+001F deterministically (short escapes for backspace/tab/LF/form-feed/CR, otherwise lowercase `\u00xx`); leaves other valid Unicode as UTF-8 without global normalization; and rejects duplicate keys, invalid Unicode/surrogates, NaN/infinity, binary floats, and booleans where integers are required. Integers use minimal base-10 with zero exactly `0`; fractional measured values in digested records use schema-bounded canonical decimal strings with no exponent, leading plus/zeros, trailing fractional zeros, or negative zero. Null/true/false are lowercase. A record's own digest field is omitted entirely while referenced predecessor/child/schema/artifact digests remain; SHA-256 is over these exact bytes and encoded lowercase hex. Pretty JSON is never hashed. Every language/path reuses this implementation and known ASCII/Unicode/key-order/decimal/own-digest vectors; do not use implementation-native object formatting or cite an unimplemented canonicalization standard.
- Every fractional threshold, metric, latency, FPS display, coordinate, and ranking value uses one `CanonicalDecimalV1` string. Its exact full-match grammar is `\A-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]{0,17})(?:\.[0-9]{0,8}[1-9])?\z` (or the target language's equivalent fullmatch), at most 18 integer digits, 9 fractional digits, and 29 bytes including sign/dot. Exponent, plus, leading integer zero, trailing fractional zero, bare dot, over-scale, and over-length tokens are invalid. A token whose exact numeric value is zero is valid only as `0`; reject `-0`, while negative nonzero values such as `-0.1` remain available only where that field permits negatives. Each field schema further fixes sign and numeric range. Parse to an exact signed integer coefficient plus scale and compare/order/gate using checked arbitrary-precision integer scale alignment or an exact Decimal context with traps and no rounding. Never compare strings, convert to binary float, or use locale. Known vectors include valid `0`, `0.1`, `0.000000001`, `1.1`, and permitted `-0.1`; numeric 2 versus 10 and -2 versus -10; rejected equivalent/noncanonical spellings; 9-digit scale max/one-over; huge-token rejection; and exact just-at/over gates. Schemas, qualifier aggregation, selector ranking, reports, and decision traces reuse this implementation.
- Use authoritative units and names across every adaptive-routing schema. Request/report/decision latency and cold-start values are nonnegative CanonicalDecimalV1 milliseconds named `*_latency_ms` or `*_cold_start_ms`; do not store unlabeled p50/p95/p99 numbers. Monotonic measured intervals and elapsed durations are unsigned integer nanoseconds named `*_duration_ns`; memory and byte sizes are unsigned integers named `*_bytes`; counts are unsigned integers. Unit-mismatch, second-versus-millisecond, float, overflow, display/gate divergence, and missing-unit fixtures must fail.

Reject invalid calendar dates, future timestamps where forbidden, overflow, offset/fraction/leap-second forms, reversed intervals, and one-second-over validity vectors.

title: P1 run three consented on-prem adaptive vision workflows
description:
## Objective

Observe three real, consented on-prem workflows from environment profiling through recommendation and local processing. A valid outcome is either a qualified selection that meets the preregistered profile or an explainable abstention.

## Required procedure

For each workflow freeze the workload-profile version; collect a privacy-safe EnvironmentProfile; verify assets/licenses locally; run read-only recommendation; qualify eligible bundles on that host when consent, ground truth, time, and assets allow; execute only an unchanged selected decision; strictly validate output; and record time to first result, manual interventions, failures, selected/abstained reason, SLO result, resource result, and follow-up intent.

User/site images, prompts, labels, predictions, content hashes, machine identifiers, and identifying consent references remain on-prem. Repository-owned records contain only aggregate metrics, non-sensitive schema/protocol/model-asset hashes, bounded failure categories, a non-personal owner_role_id, and consent status/scope/date. Never export hashes of user images, prompts, labels, predictions, filenames, consent tickets, or private dataset/report artifacts because they can reveal membership. Do not call one workflow three observations. If fewer than three real workflows are available, keep the issue open or blocked.

## Non-goals

- No public customer name/logo, raw support conversation, external upload, fabricated pilot, relaxed gate after seeing results, or promotion from a single run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Three distinct real workflows have complete privacy-safe run records and exact profile/decision/evidence linkage.
- Every workflow either meets its preregistered conditions or records why the router abstained/failed.
- Repeated product blockers become separate scoped Beads issues.

## Verification

title: P1 prove adaptive routing in real on-prem workflows
description:
## Objective

Define real workload/SLO profiles, observe three consented on-prem image-processing workflows, and publish an exact-scope support decision. This complements YOLOZU-ll2.10: that task studies users who already have predictions, while this epic studies local inference and routing.

## Success Criteria

- Workload profiles contain explicit task, input, quality metric/protocol, FPS/p95/memory, privacy/offline, license, and operating constraints before measurement.
- Three real workflows reach either a qualified local result or an honest abstention. Missing evidence is not backfilled.
- Customer/site images and raw outputs remain on the site unless a separate explicit consent permits a bounded artifact.
- The resulting support matrix names the measured environment/workload/runtime/task/bundle/protocol scope and does not claim universal best.
- Promotion, if any, uses the reviewed lifecycle rather than a pilot note alone.

## Mandatory guardrails

- Keep the current Stable predictions validation and evaluation lane backward compatible. This program starts as Experimental.
- Natural-language interpretation belongs to the calling AI client. YOLOZU accepts typed data; do not embed an LLM in the core runtime.
- Candidate means metadata or an adapter exists; Candidate is never a default. Experimental requires qualification for an exact task and measured environment/workload fingerprint. Stable requires a separate reviewed promotion decision.
- Never treat unknown as zero, absent, passing, supported, or qualified. If required evidence or hardware is unavailable, record hold, skip, abstention, or blocked honestly.
- Do not download models, code, or datasets during recommendation or execution. Fetching is a separate explicit action with source, license, and SHA-256 checks.
- Do not upload images, prompts, filenames, host identifiers, raw event telemetry, or user datasets. Normal inference must complete without runner-requested network access after explicitly approved assets are present. P0 uses audited code-owned runners and is not an OS network sandbox; enforced isolation is separate P1 work.
- User-declared local output may contain workspace-relative input identifiers and mask paths required by the existing predictions interface contract. Those values remain in the local output and must not enter qualification evidence, selection decisions, telemetry, logs, or public summaries.
- Do not reopen the runtime-expansion decision YOLOZU-ll2.13. If a screened candidate needs a runtime/provider outside the existing shipped and qualified surfaces, screening must return hold and create a separate evidence-backed runtime decision/task covering demand, license, real inference, CI, and maintenance. An adapter task must not add that runtime silently.
- Keep TTA and TTT research in YOLOZU-ll2.54 separate. Research bundles are not selectable by this router.
- If a CLI or MCP surface changes, update implementation, tools/manifest.json, the packaged manifest, related docs/manual, generated references, and -h/--help behavior in the same change.
- Use the term interface contract for software interfaces. Run the repository-required manifest gates and focused tests named by the task; report unavailable hardware tests as unavailable rather than passing.
- Beads parent-child edges are organizational, not completion blockers. Never claim or close an epic merely because `bd ready` lists it. Before epic close, query all exact direct children, put their ID/title/status evidence table in the epic notes, and require every mandatory child closed. A conditional child may instead remain explicitly blocked or deferred only with its named current hold/reject/unavailable evidence and a concrete reconsideration trigger; an ordinary open/ready child never satisfies the audit. The root epic performs the same audit over all five direct child epics. If any condition is unmet, leave the epic open.
acceptance_criteria: Three consented real on-prem workflows have preregistered SLOs, local evidence or honest abstention, privacy-safe outcome records, and an exact-scope support decision.
notes: 2026-08-29 direct-child audit: YOLOZU-ll2.81.4.1, .4.2, and .4.3 are all blocked on absent consented workload/profile/outcome evidence with concrete reopen triggers in child notes. The epic remains open because its three-workflow acceptance criterion is not met.

title: P1 implement reviewed Candidate Experimental Stable promotion

## Objective

Implement the maintainer CLI `yolozu promote-image-pipeline` plus one typed lifecycle service. The service requires the immutable target spec already registered and exactly current in the source channel; registration/onboarding remains the adapter task and promotion can never create or modify bundle_specs.json. It loads the canonical set, compares the echo byte-for-byte, and rejects missing/extra/duplicate profiles, stale heads/sets, a missing/non-current source pointer, or activation keys that do not exactly match each profile's bundle/artifact/environment/workload/protocol. `--help` and machine JSON output are required. Dry-run performs the same read-only gates and writes nothing. An approved operation atomically appends only the exact lifecycle assignment, then re-reads and verifies the profile/evidence bindings and projected pointer.

description:
## Objective

Implement only the backend/OS rows selected by the isolation-policy decision as one reusable IsolatedRunner service consumed by qualification and every end-user dispatcher (`process_images`, bounded streams, tracking, and OCR). Close this runner-framework task using live enforcement probes plus a repository-owned benign typed runner fixture that is incapable of becoming qualified/selectable. The first real candidate/model smoke remains in each downstream approved-adapter Bead. If the decision is none_supported or any mandatory live probe fails, do not close this task or isolated_acquisition: mark both blocked/deferred with isolation_unsupported and never substitute an in-process or ordinary subprocess path.

This Bead starts deferred to 2099-12-31 and is cleared only by the exact isolation-policy branch gate. Recheck the selected backend row at claim/start and before close; loss of a mandatory capability re-defers it.

title: P1 implement fail-closed candidate screening
description:
## Objective

Turn a scout candidate into a pass, hold, or reject screening record without executing code or weights.

## Required checks

Check immutable source revision, source integrity path, code license, weight license, dataset/evaluation license, weight source/hash procedure, local-versus-hosted boundary, task/prompt/output fit, predictions interface contract mapping, runtime/provider requirements, estimated compute/memory with source, maintenance status, and known security/supply-chain concerns. Keep human review status separate from mechanical checks.

Unknown mandatory provenance, license, local availability, interface mapping, or integrity produces hold, never pass. A candidate needing a runtime/provider outside existing shipped and qualified surfaces also remains hold until a separate evidence-backed runtime decision covers demand, license, real inference, maintainable CI, and support; screening cannot silently reopen YOLOZU-ll2.13. Reject records retain reasons and source references. Pass authorizes isolated adapter/qualification work only; it does not register, select, or promote a bundle.

Define CandidateScreeningRecord as a governed immutable interface contract with exactly `pass|hold|reject`; reserve `selected|abstained` for SelectionDecision. Add canonical `docs/schemas/candidate_screening_record.schema.json` and its byte-equivalent packaged copy at `yolozu/data/schemas/candidate_screening_record.schema.json`, then update schema governance and discovery tests. Require schema version; record ID/digest; candidate/source/immutable revision; source provenance; separate mechanical check results; exact overall status and bounded reasons; issuer claim; workflow-derived trust domain; non-personal reviewer_role_id; bounded public review reference or site-local-reference status; UTC review time; and optional supersedes_record_id/digest. Canonical repository-owned reviewed records may be yolozu_managed. Workspace/custom records are always operator_asserted regardless of their JSON fields; unknown source stays unknown. Only a current yolozu_managed pass may clear roadmap branch gates, authorize candidate acquisition, bind an onboarded bundle, or support packaged promotion.

Canonical repository screening instances append only to `yolozu/data/adaptive_routing/candidate_screening.jsonl`, which is both the source-controlled and packaged record stream. There is no second docs copy or serialized current-state index; project current records from this stream. Site/custom screening input lives only under an explicit confined path and remains operator_asserted. Append, readback, and supersession changes own only this exact stream through the repository-reviewed workflow. The complete file is capped at 8,192 records and 64 MiB before parsing/appending; exact-max is valid and one-over fails closed with `control_stream_limit_exceeded`. V1 has no pruning, compaction, rollover, or second-file suffix. Capacity exhaustion requires a separate reviewed version/migration Bead with a new stream identity and full-history compatibility plan; no loader may silently drop old records or scan only a favorable suffix.

Define one decision stream key as the digest of candidate source, immutable revision, and requested task/capability; within each key use monotonic sequence from 1 plus exact previous-record digest. Records are append-only and projection follows sequence, never timestamps. A superseding record must name the exact prior record. Loaders allow independent current records for different decision keys but reject duplicate IDs, mutable rewrites, per-key gaps/forks, dangling/wrong predecessors, cycles, or multiple current records for one key. A current yolozu_managed hold/reject immediately excludes every screened_candidate bundle bound to that stream; lifecycle revocation may follow for audit but is not required for immediate abstention.

Load CandidateScreeningRecord files only through the shared bounded JSON token reader from the P0 registry task and then strict schema validation. Screening-specific byte/count caps may be smaller, never larger; malformed/deep/duplicate-key/oversize records cannot reach trust projection or a branch gate. Implement the sole canonical provider that projects one bound candidate stream into the P0 `ScreeningEligibilityObservation`: it derives status/trust/head/record IDs from the validated canonical path, maps absence/hold/reject/untrusted/conflict/revision mismatch explicitly, and never passes source prose or lets a JSON trust claim override path/workflow provenance. Recommendation preflight calls this provider outside the pure selector; until this P1 provider exists, screened candidates receive absent and abstain.

## Non-goals

- No clone/import/execute/download, vulnerability guarantee, adapter implementation, qualification, support claim, or human-approval substitution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Canonical/packaged CandidateScreeningRecord schemas and the single source-controlled/package instance stream are covered by tests for pass, hold, reject, supersession, canonical/custom trust derivation, self-asserted managed rejection, every ScreeningEligibilityObservation mapping, exact-max/one-over byte/record caps and partial-suffix rejection, zero pure-selector file access, promoted-then-rejected abstention, reviewer-role privacy, unknown license, remote-only model, mutable revision, missing hash path, output mismatch, new-runtime hold, and unreviewed human status.
- Code, weights, and datasets have separate license fields.
- Screening output alone is rejected by the bundle registry/selector.

## Verification

Run screening schema/fixture tests, registry non-selectability tests, and git diff --check.

## Execution guardrails

- Inspect the referenced existing code and tests before editing; reuse them instead of creating a parallel implementation.

## Objective

Collect metadata about new vision algorithms from an explicit allowlist of official repositories, release pages, primary papers, and model cards. title: P1 automate evidence-gated algorithm intake and rollback
description:
## Objective

Continuously discover algorithm candidates without allowing discovered code or model metadata to become selectable automatically. Separate discovery, non-executing screening, isolated qualification, reviewed promotion, revocation, and rollback.

## Success Criteria

- Weekly monitored-source scouting is read-only, has a verified schedule/retention/missed-run policy, and records unavailable fields honestly.
- Candidate screening fails closed on provenance/license/interface/runtime uncertainty.
- Approved candidates run in a bounded isolated environment with network disabled during inference.
- Candidate to Experimental and Experimental to Stable are separate reviewed operations.
- Revocation excludes affected bundles immediately and rollback uses immutable last-known-good identities.
- Failure drills prove that hash, runtime, OOM/timeout, regression, license, and output-interface-contract failures cannot promote or silently replace a bundle.

## Mandatory guardrails

- Keep the current Stable predictions validation and evaluation lane backward compatible. This program starts as Experimental.
- Natural-language interpretation belongs to the calling AI client. YOLOZU accepts typed data; do not embed an LLM in the core runtime.
- Candidate means metadata or an adapter exists; Candidate is never a default. Experimental requires qualification for an exact task and measured environment/workload fingerprint. Stable requires a separate reviewed promotion decision.
- Never treat unknown as zero, absent, passing, supported, or qualified. If required evidence or hardware is unavailable, record hold, skip, abstention, or blocked honestly.
- Do not download models, code, or datasets during recommendation or execution. Fetching is a separate explicit action with source, license, and SHA-256 checks.
- Do not upload images, prompts, filenames, host identifiers, raw event telemetry, or user datasets. Normal inference must complete without runner-requested network access after explicitly approved assets are present. P0 uses audited code-owned runners and is not an OS network sandbox; enforced isolation is separate P1 work.
- User-declared local output may contain workspace-relative input identifiers and mask paths required by the existing predictions interface contract. Those values remain in the local output and must not enter qualification evidence, selection decisions, telemetry, logs, or public summaries.
- Do not reopen the runtime-expansion decision YOLOZU-ll2.13. If a screened candidate needs a runtime/provider outside the existing shipped and qualified surfaces, screening must return hold and create a separate evidence-backed runtime decision/task covering demand, license, real inference, CI, and maintenance. An adapter task must not add that runtime silently.
- Keep TTA and TTT research in YOLOZU-ll2.54 separate. Research bundles are not selectable by this router.
- If a CLI or MCP surface changes, update implementation, tools/manifest.json, the packaged manifest, related docs/manual, generated references, and -h/--help behavior in the same change.
- Use the term interface contract for software interfaces. Run the repository-required manifest gates and focused tests named by the task; report unavailable hardware tests as unavailable rather than passing.
- Beads parent-child edges are organizational, not completion blockers. Never claim or close an epic merely because `bd ready` lists it. Before epic close, query all exact direct children, put their ID/title/status evidence table in the epic notes, and require every mandatory child closed. A conditional child may instead remain explicitly blocked or deferred only with its named current hold/reject/unavailable evidence and a concrete reconsideration trigger; an ordinary open/ready child never satisfies the audit. The root epic performs the same audit over all five direct child epics. If any condition is unmet, leave the epic open.

title: P1 onboard and qualify initial algorithm bundles
description:
## Objective

Represent existing baselines in the new registry, screen one text-prompted detection/segmentation family and one low-latency closed-set family, implement only candidates that pass screening, and collect measured CPU, Apple Silicon, and NVIDIA evidence when those real hosts are legitimately available.

## Success Criteria

- Existing models are registered without inventing performance or maturity.
- Candidate decisions pin primary sources, revisions, code/weight licenses, hashes or hash acquisition procedure, prompt/output semantics, runtime requirements, and predictions interface contract mapping before code is copied or weights are downloaded.
- Optional adapters do not break core installation and enter as Candidate only.
- Measured reports never generalize beyond matching environment/workload/protocol fingerprints; unavailable hardware remains blocked rather than backfilled.
- Each platform baseline task freezes its exact bundle-ID set before running. Each newly implemented candidate has a separate qualification task, so a baseline-only run cannot be mistaken for candidate evidence.

## Mandatory guardrails

- Keep the current Stable predictions validation and evaluation lane backward compatible. This program starts as Experimental.
- Natural-language interpretation belongs to the calling AI client. YOLOZU accepts typed data; do not embed an LLM in the core runtime.
- Candidate means metadata or an adapter exists; Candidate is never a default. Experimental requires qualification for an exact task and measured environment/workload fingerprint. Stable requires a separate reviewed promotion decision.
- Never treat unknown as zero, absent, passing, supported, or qualified. If required evidence or hardware is unavailable, record hold, skip, abstention, or blocked honestly.
- Do not download models, code, or datasets during recommendation or execution. Fetching is a separate explicit action with source, license, and SHA-256 checks.
- Do not upload images, prompts, filenames, host identifiers, raw event telemetry, or user datasets. Normal inference must complete without runner-requested network access after explicitly approved assets are present. P0 uses audited code-owned runners and is not an OS network sandbox; enforced isolation is separate P1 work.

title: P2 define the OCR result interface contract
description:
## Objective

Define a dedicated versioned OCR result interface contract before adding an OCR adapter. OCR text must not be forced into detection class labels.

## Required semantics

Define recognized text, one exact quadrilateral, separate `detection_confidence` and `recognition_confidence`, script/language status, logical input_image_index, optional logical_page_reference, and model/component provenance. Each confidence is a finite CanonicalDecimalV1 from 0 through 1; do not invent a combined/product/minimum confidence. The immutable OCR bundle declares `language_ids` with 1..256 entries, `script_ids` with 1..128 entries, and `ocr_components` with exactly two records whose roles are exactly detector and recognizer. Every ID is one 1..64-byte ASCII token matching `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}`; IDs are distinct within each array, component IDs are distinct, and each component record has exact distinct component_id and model_id. Across the runner/isolation boundary, only detected language and script are runner-controlled: each is an integral in-range index into its matching array or exact `unknown`. Core maps indices and rejects arbitrary strings or invalid indices. Component/model provenance never comes from the runner and never permits unknown; core stamps the exact selected detector/recognizer component_id/model_id from the pinned bundle after output validation.

Geometry is exactly four distinct ordered semantic corners `top_left,top_right,bottom_right,bottom_left` in clockwise image-coordinate order, with eight finite CanonicalDecimalV1 coordinates within decoded bounds. Require a strict convex, non-self-intersecting quadrilateral with nonzero positive shoelace area; reject duplicate, collinear, concave, self-intersecting, wrong-start, or wrong-winding forms rather than rotating/reordering them. Arbitrary polygons are not accepted in v1. Bound canonical geometry encoding to 512 UTF-8 bytes per item and 64 MiB per job, counted before cross-isolation return/JSON assembly; reject overflow rather than truncate. `input_image_index` is an integer from 0 through job image_count-1. `logical_page_reference` is exactly null or an integer 1..2,147,483,647, at most one per decoded input; it is display-only and never affects paths, decoding, input indexing, or selection. Reject index/page mismatch.

Every OCR result carries fixed `content_trust=untrusted_input_derived`; recognized text is attacker-controlled image-derived data and must never be interpreted as instructions, tool arguments, paths, URLs to fetch, or registry/job settings. Reading order and orientation are optional and can be unknown. The first OCR lane accepts only the existing bounded JPEG, PNG, and single-frame WebP image inputs; it does not parse PDF, TIFF, animated/multipage images, archives, office documents, or video. V1 component_mode is exactly detect_and_recognize. Empty success is valid only when both pinned components complete successfully and the detector returns zero regions. A detector/recognizer timeout, crash, missing component, or invalid output is a stable failure with no partial result publication and cannot qualify; it is never converted to empty/no-text. Define privacy-safe summaries with no recognized content.

Preserve legitimate recognized Unicode exactly without semantic normalization. Require valid UTF-8 and reject NUL and lone UTF-16 surrogate code points. Bound each recognized item to 4,096 Unicode code points and 16,384 UTF-8 bytes, each image to 1,000 items and 1 MiB recognized UTF-8, and one job to 100,000 items and 64 MiB recognized UTF-8. Count and reject before JSON assembly/output overflow; never truncate silently.

Recognized text is inert user-owned output data and must not appear in MCP/job summaries, SelectionDecision, telemetry, benchmark summaries, generic errors, support logs, or downstream actions. title: P2 screen the first local tracking candidate

Tracking-by-detection is a bounded extension of the detector pipeline and can improve stream efficiency without introducing identity recognition. title: P2 extend adaptive routing interface contracts for tracking
description:
## Objective

Add a versioned tracking routing extension before any tracker implementation. Preserve every static-image v1 validator, reason code, MCP request, and output unchanged.

## Exact extension surfaces

Add canonical `docs/schemas/tracking_job_spec.schema.json`, `tracking_bundle_extension.schema.json`, `tracking_qualification_report.schema.json`, and `tracking_selection_decision.schema.json`, with same-basename packaged copies. TrackingJobSpec composes the bounded Stream request with tracker task, session/cadence mode, the exact `tracking_latency_interval_id`, and an optional complete quality requirement containing exact metric, direction, evaluation-dataset ID/digest, protocol digest, evaluation-vocabulary/class mapping, tracking task semantics, and finite threshold; accuracy_first requires it. Tracking bundle capability declares detector/tracker component identities, observation/prediction semantics, state/reset behavior, and detection cadence. Tracking latency starts at the same source due(i) as Stream latency and ends only after detector result handoff, tracker update/state mutation, tracking postprocess, strict TrackingResult/link validation, any mask write, and synchronous canonical append of that frame's tracking rows to the managed staging file. The incremental writer has at most 1,048,576 bytes of scratch, performs no third queue/drop policy, empties its frame scratch before returning, and a slow/blocked write remains inside latency and the job deadline. Bind writer ID/version/encoding/scratch cap to workload/protocol/report/decision; timeout or partial append fails atomically. It is distinct from and never substituted by the earlier detection FrameResult latency. Tracking qualification binds that interval and the exact same quality comparability key, and adds preregistered HOTA/IDF1/MOTA/ID-switch fields with explicit directions plus measured sustained drop/queue/tracking p50/p95/p99 and whole-job memory scope; unknown, stream-only, or cross-dataset/protocol metrics never pass a gate.

Define whole tracking-job memory as the peak aggregate over unique processes/cgroups and code-owned buffers from source start through teardown: orchestrator, decoder, detector runner/sandbox, tracker runner/sandbox, every descendant, frame/callback/tracking queues and pools, state, masks, and output staging. Accelerator memory covers all participating processes/devices. Bind collector ID/version/scope in workload/protocol/report. If complete non-double-counted coverage is unavailable, memory is unknown and cannot pass a hard gate; wrapper-only or tracker-only memory is invalid.

Extend selector dispatch with tracking task/capability/dataset/metric/direction/protocol/vocabulary/cadence/tracking-latency/memory-collector mismatches and require active trusted TrackingQualificationReport evidence. Direction-aware ranking is descending for HOTA/IDF1/MOTA-style higher-is-better and ascending for ID-switch/error-style lower-is-better after exact comparability match. Stream-only p95/memory evidence is ineligible. TrackingSelectionDecision embeds the complete StreamSelectionDecision source binding, including local-only stream_source_digest and MP4 length/hash or unique-camera capability semantics, plus the tracking interval/collector/report identities; `process_tracking_stream` redoes the same pinned-handle or exact-one-camera check and rejects generic StreamSelectionDecision/cross-kind decisions. Add canonical Experimental MCP tools `recommend_tracking_pipeline` and asynchronous `process_tracking_stream`; the latter reuses the extended jobs_status/jobs_cancel protocol and the shared concurrency-one/no-pending stream slot. Dispatch code_owned_audited versus third_party_isolated through the same P0/IsolatedRunner trust gate. Use ManagedOutputTransaction for exactly `detector_frame_results.jsonl`, `tracking_results.jsonl`, `stream_summary.json`, `provenance.json`, `checksums.json`, and at most 9,999 declared mask artifacts, so the inherited total remains at most 10,004 files and 4 GiB. The streaming writer stores every processed complete canonical validated FrameResult exactly once in detector_frame_results.jsonl, then appends bounded observed/predicted/lost/ended tracking rows; observed rows refer to the exact frame_result_digest/result index and individual detector results may remain unreferenced. The post-stage strict streaming validator rechecks both files and rejects tampered, missing, duplicate, dangling, cross-frame, or mismatched references before publication. Write/validate potentially large rows incrementally rather than constructing one unbounded DOM. Apply the independent FrameResult-line, contained-detector-result, per-frame tracking-row, and nonresetting job-wide tracking-row-plus-state caps before append; only mask/file/byte caps are shared. stream_summary.json includes the distinct tracking interval ID and aggregate tracking p50/p95/p99/memory, but remains runtime status rather than qualification evidence. checksums.json lists every other declared file and never itself. - No tracker algorithm, stream engine rewrite, biometric identity, unversioned change to v1, public qualified bundle, or automatic cadence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Interface-contract fixtures cover task, component, cadence, all three indices/reset/modulo/link semantics, exact dataset/metric/direction/protocol/vocabulary/task-semantics, higher- and lower-is-better ordering, active tracking evidence, tracking interval/writer/whole-job-memory collector and stream-only-evidence rejection, slow-writer/backpressure/scratch max+1/timeout with no third queue or partial publication, embedded stream_source_digest and source replacement, unique/ambiguous camera binding, shared stream_busy/cancel/dry-run behavior, trust-class isolation dispatch, output-kind, retained FrameResult own-digest/source-link validation, incremental per-frame/session/job max/one-over rows/state, tamper/dangling/missing/duplicate source records, and backward-compatible static v1 paths.
- test_only=true always rejects on public recommendation/execution. Pure-selector tests pass a nonpackaged in-memory trusted test_only=false tracking spec directly to the pure function; executor-only tests inject a fake tracking runner below the public routing gate. Neither fixture is loadable through registry/MCP or called a selected end-to-end test. Public defaults abstain and v1 output remains byte-compatible.
- Canonical/packaged schemas, source/packaged manifests, MCP live schema, generated reference, docs, and help agree.

## Verification

Run tracking routing/selector/MCP/output/backward-compatibility tests, schema governance, required manifest gates, generated-reference check, and git diff --check.

## Execution guardrails

- Inspect the referenced existing code and tests before editing; reuse them instead of creating a parallel implementation.
- Make the smallest additive change that satisfies this issue. Do not change public behavior outside this scope.
- Do not make a Stable support claim from fixtures, synthetic timing, public model-card numbers, or a successful import.
- Missing optional dependencies or target hardware must produce an explicit skip, hold, abstention, or blocked state; do not fabricate a successful path.
- Every adaptive-routing digest reuses one code-owned `canonical_json_v1` implementation. It emits UTF-8 with no BOM/whitespace; preserves array order; sorts object keys by their UTF-8 byte sequence; escapes quote, backslash, and U+0000..U+001F deterministically (short escapes for backspace/tab/LF/form-feed/CR, otherwise lowercase `\u00xx`); leaves other valid Unicode as UTF-8 without global normalization; and rejects duplicate keys, invalid Unicode/surrogates, NaN/infinity, binary floats, and booleans where integers are required. Integers use minimal base-10 with zero exactly `0`; fractional measured values in digested records use schema-bounded canonical decimal strings with no exponent, leading plus/zeros, trailing fractional zeros, or negative zero. Null/true/false are lowercase. A record's own digest field is omitted entirely while referenced predecessor/child/schema/artifact digests remain; SHA-256 is over these exact bytes and encoded lowercase hex. Pretty JSON is never hashed. Every language/path reuses this implementation and known ASCII/Unicode/key-order/decimal/own-digest vectors; do not use implementation-native object formatting or cite an unimplemented canonicalization standard.
- Every fractional threshold, metric, latency, FPS display, coordinate, and ranking value uses one `CanonicalDecimalV1` string. Its exact full-match grammar is `\A-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]{0,17})(?:\.[0-9]{0,8}[1-9])?\z` (or the target language's equivalent fullmatch), at most 18 integer digits, 9 fractional digits, and 29 bytes including sign/dot.
