A token whose exact numeric value is zero is valid only as `0`; reject `-0`, while negative nonzero values such as `-0.1` remain available only where that field permits negatives. Each field schema further fixes sign and numeric range. Parse to an exact signed integer coefficient plus scale and compare/order/gate using checked arbitrary-precision integer scale alignment or an exact Decimal context with traps and no rounding. Never compare strings, convert to binary float, or use locale. Known vectors include valid `0`, `0.1`, `0.000000001`, `1.1`, and permitted `-0.1`; numeric 2 versus 10 and -2 versus -10; rejected equivalent/noncanonical spellings; 9-digit scale max/one-over; huge-token rejection; and exact just-at/over gates. Schemas, qualifier aggregation, selector ranking, reports, and decision traces reuse this implementation.
- Use authoritative units and names across every adaptive-routing schema. Request/report/decision latency and cold-start values are nonnegative CanonicalDecimalV1 milliseconds named `*_latency_ms` or `*_cold_start_ms`; do not store unlabeled p50/p95/p99 numbers. Monotonic measured intervals and elapsed durations are unsigned integer nanoseconds named `*_duration_ns`; memory and byte sizes are unsigned integers named `*_bytes`; counts are unsigned integers. Throughput/FPS gating is authoritative from an integer processed/sample count and integer duration_ns exact ratio; an optional CanonicalDecimalV1 display is rounded only for display by a fixed documented rule and is excluded from digests, comparisons, and gates. Unit-mismatch, second-versus-millisecond, float, overflow, display/gate divergence, and missing-unit fixtures must fail.
- Every persisted UTC instant uses exact RFC3339 UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`: four-digit year, valid Gregorian calendar date, two-digit fields, no offset, fractional second, leap second, or alternate spelling. Parse and compare instants rather than strings. Evidence validity is at most exactly `90 * 86400` seconds after report completion; monotonic duration_ns is separate and never derived by subtracting wall-clock strings. Reject invalid calendar dates, future timestamps where forbidden, overflow, offset/fraction/leap-second forms, reversed intervals, and one-second-over validity vectors.

It lists every other declared regular file with exact relative path, size, and SHA-256 plus the expected path set/count/total bytes; it never lists itself. Cover the manifest through the enclosing record/output digest when one exists, and test rejection of self-entry, missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, or mismatched entries.

title: P2 define the tracking output interface contract
description:
## Objective

Define a versioned tracking extension without silently changing the existing predictions interface contract.

## Required semantics

A lost track may reappear with the same ID until an explicit ended transition; once ended, that ID is never reused in the same session. A reset terminates the old session and starts a new session in which IDs may restart. Bound emitted tracking rows in one frame to exact `max_results_per_frame` (at most 1,000), active tracks to 1,000, and unique IDs/state records within one session to 1,000,000. Also maintain one job-wide monotonic budget counter that increments for every emitted tracking row and every first allocation of a state record; it never resets on session reset and must remain at most 1,000,000. Reject before emitting or allocating the max+1 item. Ending/resetting a track releases active memory but never refunds either the session-unique or job-wide accounting.

Separate indices exactly. `source_frame_index` is the job-wide integer 0..863,999, never reused, and equals the source Stream FrameResult index. `session_index` is 0..863,999 and increments exactly once on reset. `session_frame_index` is 0..863,999, starts at 0 for each session, and increments for each processed source frame in that session. Cadence uses only `session_frame_index % detector_interval`; it never resets or aliases source_frame_index. A row with state=observed must carry an `observation_ref` with the exact source FrameResult `frame_result_digest` plus one integral source-result index in range. If it copies source bbox/mask/class/score fields, those copies must exactly match the referenced result. Tracker-adjusted geometry/state is represented separately in a typed `track_estimate` field with explicit tracker-estimate source semantics, allowing one track row per frame without pretending the estimate equals the raw detection. A row with state=predicted must omit observation_ref and any copied detection fields. Reject dangling, cross-frame, duplicate, mismatched-copy, or predicted-with-link rows. Individual detector results may legitimately remain unreferenced. The strict streaming validator first verifies every FrameResult own digest from its canonical bytes, then verifies every tracking reference and optional copied field; online-only validation or an unretained callback object is insufficient. FrameResult-line count, contained detector-result count, and tracking-row-plus-state count are independent governed caps. Only the aggregate mask-artifact, output-file, and 4-GiB output-byte caps are shared across both files and provenance.

Freeze the v1 state machine. TrackingJobSpec and the bundle/workload/report bind integer `max_prediction_frames` and `max_lost_frames`, each 0..240. Row state is exactly `observed|predicted|lost|ended`; do not define parallel detector_observation/tracker_prediction row kinds. A new ID can start only as observed. An observed row requires observation_ref and a typed track_estimate; any copied detector fields must match. A predicted row requires track_estimate and forbids observation_ref/copied detector fields. A lost or ended row forbids observation_ref, detector copies, geometry/mask, score, and track_estimate. From observed or predicted, the next row may be observed; predicted only when its resulting consecutive prediction count is at most max_prediction_frames; lost only when its resulting consecutive lost count (starting at one) is at most max_lost_frames; otherwise it must be ended. From lost, the next row may be observed reappearance, lost only when its resulting consecutive lost count is at most max_lost_frames, or ended. Thus max_lost_frames=0 never emits lost, and max_prediction_frames=0 never emits predicted. Ended is terminal and never reappears. Observed, predicted, and lost IDs all remain reserved and cannot be assigned to another track. Every non-ended track emits exactly one row on every processed frame, rows are ordered by track_id ascending, and no track has two rows in one frame. A reset, EOF, cancellation, or terminal job failure writes one bounded session-termination record with reason and active/lost counts and terminates every remaining ID without synthesizing per-track ended rows; a later reset starts a new session/index namespace. The entire frame row batch, counters, and state update validate against all caps before any append/mutation; cap overflow fails the job atomically rather than dropping/reordering tracks. Use exact monotonic frame/due timestamps and confidence/source fields that distinguish observation, estimate, prediction, and lifecycle-only rows.

Explicitly exclude person identification, face recognition, biometric inference, cross-camera or cross-session identity linking, and persistent identity databases.

- Privacy and identity non-goals are explicit in docs/schema.

title: P2 implement the bounded local stream engine
description:
## Objective

Expose one shared asynchronous service and canonical Experimental MCP tool `process_local_stream`. With explicit dry_run=false it validates and submits one bounded local video/camera job, returns promptly with `job_id` plus a workspace-relative output reference, and reuses the existing canonical `jobs_status` and `jobs_cancel` tools for observation/cancellation. Do not add a separate CLI or parallel job protocol in this task. Across `process_local_stream`, `process_tracking_stream`, and future stream-derived tools, one server/workspace permits concurrency exactly 1 and pending capacity 0; while any stream job is queued/running, a second submission returns stream_busy before creating a job record or opening a source. Process the source through an unchanged selected bundle using a bounded queue and deterministic block/drop_oldest behavior.

## Required behavior

Accept only a validated StreamSelectionDecision; reject generic static, tracking, OCR, or other decision kinds before any source/runner action. dry_run=true is synchronous read-only preflight: it validates decision, registry/evidence/artifacts, paths, and policy. For MP4 it may safe-open no-follow, hash and bounded-parse the exact stat-stable file, then closes the handle; for camera it only enumerates and never opens/captures. It then returns without full decode, decoder/runner/sandbox/output calls, job submission, job ID/record, semaphore reservation, or filesystem mutation. Only dry_run=false may pass the stream_busy gate and submit. For MP4 execution, safe-open a no-follow pinned handle, hash the exact bytes/length, require its stream_source_digest to match, and decode only from that same stat-stable handle. For camera, re-enumerate exactly one eligible device and require the canonical provider/capability-request digest to match before opening; never persist a device ID. Reuse P0 artifact-state, lifecycle/evidence, workspace, and exact-managed-force checks; no job may substitute the source, bundle, evidence, or artifact set after queuing. Dispatch code_owned_audited only through its allowlisted host runner and third_party_isolated only through the live IsolatedRunner matching policy/image digest; never host-import isolated candidate code. Never exceed configured frame-queue count/decoded bytes, callback count/serialized bytes, or any frozen stream/output cap, including during allocation. Implement queued/start, normal EOF, stop-at-cap, active cancellation, consumer_backpressure, invalid frame, camera disconnect, runner failure, and timeout cleanup. Release camera/decoder/runner/output resources and the shared stream slot exactly once on every path.

Extend the existing shared JobManager rather than wrapping it with a parallel registry. Preserve current non-stream behavior, but add a cooperative cancellation token that reaches active stream source/decoder, both bounded queues, host runner or IsolatedRunner, and output transaction. `jobs_cancel` must cancel queued work and signal running stream work. It never serializes a binary-float drop fraction. This runtime StreamSummary is user-owned aggregate status/output only; it is not a QualificationReport, cannot be activated, and cannot enter selector evidence. checksums.json lists every other declared file with exact path/size/hash and never itself; reject undeclared/symlink/path-escaping files and use the shared recovery/force rules. title: P2 define streaming image-processing interface contracts
description:
## Objective

Define versioned request, result, and evidence extensions for bounded local streaming before implementing a stream loop.

## Required semantics

Represent source type, resolution, exact source-rate rational, minimum sustained processing FPS, maximum end-to-end p95, queue count and decoded-byte bounds, drop policy, finite max-drop rational and max_consecutive_drops, timeout, maximum duration, maximum frames, cancellation, output cadence, per-frame result cap, total-result cap, decoder memory cap, and output byte/file caps. Initial source scope is a workspace-confined local MP4 file containing H.264/AVC 8-bit 4:2:0, or a local camera exposed through a code-owned allowlisted provider; reject other containers/codecs/providers until a versioned extension. Source rate uses reduced integers `source_rate_num=1..240000` and `source_rate_den=1..1001` with quotient 0.1..240 and must exactly match MP4 metadata or the requested/negotiated camera capability. V1 never intentionally samples frames. Both sources use a rational monotonic schedule `due(i)=start+i*source_rate_den/source_rate_num`, evaluated by checked integer cross-multiplication with no cumulative binary-float rounding or busy wait. For MP4, validate constant monotonic PTS, reject VFR/duplicate/regressing/gapped timestamps and incompatible edit lists, and permit before due time only bounded compressed packet/index prefetch; native decode, DPB/decoded allocation, and queue reservation for frame i start no earlier than due(i). For camera, allocate the complete fixed-count/fixed-byte ingress pool before starting, require the code-owned provider to fill only caller-supplied pool buffers, emit one monotonically indexed tick for every negotiated due time, and explicitly report a missed tick as dropped; hidden provider buffers or unreported device drops are unsupported. The governed latency start for both sources is due(i), so buffer/admission/decode lateness cannot be hidden. Unpaced/full-speed MP4 runs are batch diagnostic only and cannot emit or satisfy StreamQualificationReport/selection evidence. Bind `source_admission_policy_id/version` into the workload/protocol. Every scheduled source index is processed, dropped, or explicit failed_unaccounted under the declared policy.

Define backpressure exactly. Compute checked worst-case decoded bytes as `width * 4 * height` from preflight/negotiated dimensions. MP4 reserves that amount plus one queue slot at or after due(i) before native decode allocation; camera reserves the whole ingress pool before start and logically assigns one already-counted buffer at each due(i). After strict frame validation, only a smaller exact `stride_bytes * height` may release excess. `block` waits for both reservations without allocating/decoding another frame and records zero drops; its wait remains inside due-to-result latency. `drop_oldest` evicts oldest queued decoded frames in ascending source-frame index until both count and byte bounds can hold the worst-case reservation, and records every evicted or provider-reported missed index as dropped. Dropped and processed indices are mutually exclusive. Consecutive drops are maximal adjacent source-frame-index runs, including evictions at EOF; at EOF/cancel/timeout, queued but unprocessed frames are deterministically drained within the remaining deadline or counted as dropped for drop_oldest, while block terminates failed/unaccounted rather than relabeling them as drops. No scheduled frame may disappear from `processed + dropped + explicit failed_unaccounted`, and any failed_unaccounted count makes qualification ineligible. Authoritative drop_fraction is the integer ratio `dropped / (processed + dropped)` over accounted scheduled frames; a zero denominator is failed/unknown, never zero. The hard maximum is canonical reduced `max_drop_num/max_drop_den`, with denominator 1..1,000,000, numerator 0..denominator, gcd=1, and zero represented only as 0/1; compare by checked integer cross-multiplication without float/decimal rounding. A six-decimal half-even display string may be emitted but is excluded from identity/gating. block requires zero dropped frames. max_consecutive_drops is an integer 0..864,000; both drop gates are hard. Record frame index, monotonic processing timestamp, optional device timestamp, processed/dropped/failed-unaccounted counts, maximum consecutive drops, count/decoded-byte queue high-water marks, and termination reason.

Output cadence is exactly one FrameResult for every processed frame, including a valid empty-results row; dropped frames emit no FrameResult and appear only in aggregate counts. Every FrameResult carries `frame_result_digest = SHA256(canonical_json_v1(the complete FrameResult with only its own digest field omitted))`. Strict validation creates one canonical byte sequence, computes the digest, and uses those same validated bytes for the callback and JSONL line; it never digests a file checksum, pretty JSON, or a partial result. Downstream `source_frame_result_digest` means only this field. End-to-end latency for both MP4 and camera starts at the frame's rational scheduled due(i), before buffer acquisition/decode/capture. It ends only after admission/backpressure, demux/decode or capture, frame-queue wait, preprocess, inference, postprocess, strict result/mask validation and bounded mask write, plus successful callback-buffer enqueue. Qualification and execution bind and use this identical latency-interval ID. Device-supplied capture/ready timestamps may be diagnostic but never substitute for the governed p95.

Every stream call is capped by the remaining overall job deadline and these smaller ceilings: source/container probe or camera enumeration/open 10 seconds; first camera frame 10 seconds; runner probe 30 seconds; runner/sandbox load 600 seconds; each frame decode 5 seconds; each predict 30 seconds; each bounded mask/output/callback step 30 seconds; and close 10 seconds. Cancellation has a 5-second cooperative grace, then terminates/reaps the bounded native child process group. Stable reasons are source_probe_timeout, camera_open_timeout, camera_frame_timeout, runner_probe_timeout, runner_load_timeout, decode_timeout, predict_timeout, output_timeout, close_timeout, cancelled, and cancellation_forced. A timeout never becomes a drop/skip or qualified SLO sample.

For MP4, require a no-follow regular file at most 8 GiB. Before full decode, a code-owned parser/probe gets at most 10 seconds, 64 MiB input bytes, 100,000 boxes/atoms, and nesting depth 32. Require exactly one enabled video track and zero audio, subtitle, metadata, attachment, or other tracks; codec/profile/pixel format, declared dimensions, duration, frame count/rate, constant-duration PTS schedule, rotation, and edit list must be known and internally consistent with every stream cap. Allow only H.264 Constrained Baseline, Main, or High, 8-bit 4:2:0, level 3.0 through 5.1, at most 16 reference frames, checked decoded-picture-buffer bytes at most 536,870,912, GOP at most 600 frames, MP4 video sample/packet at most 67,108,864 bytes, and individual NAL unit at most 33,554,432 bytes. Reject unknown-duration/frame-count, VFR or invalid PTS, unsupported profile/level/DPB/reference/GOP/sample/NAL, fragmented/live, encrypted/DRM, external-reference, attachment, malformed/overlapping atom, parser-bomb, and extra-track files. Full parsing/decoding runs in a code-owned bounded child/cgroup with hard `max_decoder_rss_bytes` required in 67,108,864..2,147,483,648, no network/secrets, bounded IPC, and enforced before reading a full sample or constructing the decoder. If the current OS/backend cannot enforce the hard process-tree/cgroup limit, return decoder_backend_unsupported; exceeding sample/DPB/RSS returns decoder_sample_limit, decoder_dpb_limit, or decoder_memory_limit, terminates/reaps the child, and never falls back in-process. Keep the same open file descriptor and verify stat stability through decode; never reopen by path. Camera preflight uses a code-owned enumeration API without capturing frames and requires exactly one eligible device for the allowlisted provider/capability request at recommendation and again immediately before execution; zero or two-plus causes camera_binding_ambiguous abstention. Only providers supporting the bounded preallocated pool above are allowed. Never persist/return a device identifier. This v1 binds the unique eligible provider/capability source, not physical identity; multiple same-capability cameras require a future session-scoped opaque lease interface contract.

Freeze v1 bounds: `min_sustained_fps` is a finite canonical decimal in 0.1..240 and is only an SLO gate, never a source pacing/sampling request; queue capacity 1..64; max_queued_decoded_bytes 1..536,870,912 (512 MiB); decoded width/height 1..8,192 and at most 33,177,600 pixels per frame; max_duration_seconds 1..3,600; max_frames 1..864,000; configured max_results_per_frame 1..1,000; at most 1,000,000 contained task-result entries across all FrameResults, 10,000 mask artifacts, 10,004 output files, and 4 GiB declared output total. Validate by checked rational arithmetic that `max_frames >= ceil(source_rate_num * required_duration_seconds / source_rate_den)`; a soft-real-time qualification uses required_duration_seconds at least 600 and rejects before source open if its duration/frame caps cannot cover the full soak. `stream_results.jsonl` has a separate line cap equal to the maximum processed-frame count, at most 864,000; each line is exactly one FrameResult and its contained task-result entries count toward the independent 1,000,000 total. The queue representation is validated uint8 three-channel RGB/BGR with positive stride at least width*3 and at most width*4; calculate both worst-case `width*4*height` before allocation and exact `stride_bytes * height` after decode using checked arithmetic. One worst-case frame must fit max_queued_decoded_bytes. Enforce both queue count and aggregate decoded bytes before allocation/enqueue; drop/block according to policy without temporary over-cap storage. A downstream callback buffer is separately bounded at 64 FrameResult items and 67,108,864 serialized bytes; compute each validated result's canonical byte size before enqueue. It uses blocking backpressure only and never drops a second time; if it cannot drain within the remaining job deadline, terminate consumer_backpressure without exceeding either bound. Mask payloads never hide outside these budgets: validate mask dimensions/pixels against the frame, cap each encoded mask at 67,108,864 bytes, and stream it synchronously in at most 1-MiB chunks into the bounded managed-output stage before enqueuing its small FrameResult reference/size/hash. No callback or frame queue retains mask bytes; aggregate mask bytes count toward the 4-GiB output cap. A tracking consumer receives only the validated read-only reference and must not cause a second in-memory mask copy/queue. Stop at the first duration/frame/result/file/byte cap and report the exact bounded termination reason; no zero, omitted, or unlimited sentinel. Define a versioned FrameResult record for detections/mask references plus frame metadata and an aggregate StreamSummary. A frame may legitimately contain zero actual results. Per-frame results are user-owned output, not qualification telemetry.

Raw frames, source credentials, filenames, camera identifiers, and per-frame raw telemetry must not enter summaries/logs. State that the SLO is measured soft real-time, not a hard real-time guarantee. RTSP/network URLs are invalid in this version.

## Non-goals

- No stream engine, tracker, OCR, RTSP, codec expansion, hard real-time claim, or unbounded queue.

Define exact canonical schemas for stream_job_spec, stream_workload_profile, frame_result, stream_summary, stream_qualification_report, and stream_selection_decision under `docs/schemas/`, with same-basename packaged copies. StreamJobSpec/StreamWorkloadProfile/evidence/selection all bind exact source-rate rational, source-admission scheduler ID/version, one-result-row-per-processed-frame cadence, max_results_per_frame/total rows, queue count, max_queued_decoded_bytes, camera-pool/decoded-layout/stride policy, drop policy/max rational/consecutive limit, mask encoding ID, per-mask/chunk/total output limits, hard max_decoder_rss_bytes, and one decoder-policy digest covering backend/enforcement plus the exact H.264 profile/level/reference/DPB/GOP/sample/NAL caps, and the governed latency interval. Any cap/backend/policy mismatch rejects evidence. Define `stream_job_peak_rss_bytes` over the unique whole job from source start through teardown: orchestrator, decoder child/cgroup, host or isolated runner and every descendant, camera/frame/callback queues and pools, masks, and output staging. Accelerator memory covers every participating process/device. Bind exact memory collector ID/version/source/scope to workload/protocol/report/decision and aggregate without double-counting shared cgroups; incomplete coverage is unknown and cannot pass a hard memory gate. Base image-runner-only RSS never substitutes. Any stream quality gate also binds exact metric, direction, evaluation-dataset ID/digest, protocol digest, and evaluation-vocabulary/task semantics. StreamQualificationReport extends the immutable bundle/artifact/environment/protocol evidence rules with exact source kind/codec/resolution/rate/admission/decoder policy/cadence/result/mask limits, queue/drop policy and both high-water marks, duration/frame counts, p50/p95/p99, authoritative processed/dropped/failed-unaccounted integers plus max-consecutive drops, job-wide memory, thermal/power status, and termination. A static-image QualificationReport cannot substitute for stream evidence.

Define sustained FPS without a binary float. After all declared warm-up, the governed sustained section starts at the next source due instant and ends at a monotonic instant at least 600 seconds later; store integer `sustained_duration_ns` and the count of strictly validated FrameResults completed within that interval. The authoritative rate is `processed_frames * 1_000_000_000 / sustained_duration_ns`; dropped, failed, warm-up, and post-section drain frames are not in the numerator. Compare to the finite canonical-decimal min_sustained_fps by exact scaled-integer cross-multiplication. An optional six-decimal half-even display string is excluded from identity/gating. Zero duration/count, failed_unaccounted, early termination, or mixed admitted/processed counts is failed/unknown, never zero FPS.

StreamSelectionDecision contains a sensitive local-only `stream_source_digest`. For MP4 it is canonical_json_v1/SHA-256 over source kind, exact byte length, and SHA-256 of the exact bytes read from the pinned no-follow handle. For camera it binds only the canonical allowlisted provider/capability request (format, dimensions, rate) plus eligible_device_count exactly one, and never a persistent device ID; execution re-enumerates exactly one eligible device or fails camera_binding_ambiguous before open. This digest may appear only in the returned decision and user-owned local provenance, never qualification evidence, logs, telemetry, or public summaries. It is a separate decision kind; static SelectionDecision and other task variants are invalid inputs to stream execution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Python/JSON interface contracts have matching valid/invalid fixtures for both policies, every numeric/source/container/probe/track/codec/result/file/byte/decoder-memory limit, rate/admission/cadence/latency interval, timestamps, cancellation, and failure reasons. Slow-consumer fixtures reach frame-queue and callback item/byte bounds without OOM or second-stage drops; exact-max/one-over mask size/count/total and chunked no-in-flight-copy behavior, max/one-over stride/result-byte arithmetic, consumer_backpressure, zero/ambiguous camera eligibility, preallocated camera pool and hidden-buffer/unreported-drop rejection, zero-frame drop fraction, canonical 0/1 and 1/3 plus 0/0/non-reduced/just-at/over rational gates, exact drop_oldest eviction until both count/byte capacity fit, source-index consecutive runs including EOF, block reservation before allocation with due-time latency, failed-unaccounted ineligibility, constant-PTS paced MP4 with no pre-due native decode and VFR/gap/regression/full-speed-evidence rejection, H.264 sample/NAL/profile/level/reference/DPB/GOP max and one-over plus enforced decoder RSS/unsupported backend, source-rate/frame-cap cross-field mismatch/no-sampling, and fast-but-over-drop candidates fail deterministically.
- FrameResult fixtures verify own-digest omission, known canonical hash vectors, tamper rejection, exact callback/JSONL canonical-byte identity, and unambiguous downstream source_frame_result_digest linking.
- Invalid/unbounded/network sources fail closed.
- Existing static ImageJobSpec and predictions interface contract remain backward compatible.

## Verification

Run focused interface-contract/schema-governance tests and git diff --check.

## Execution guardrails

- Inspect the referenced existing code and tests before editing; reuse them instead of creating a parallel implementation.
- Make the smallest additive change that satisfies this issue. Do not change public behavior outside this scope.
- Do not make a Stable support claim from fixtures, synthetic timing, public model-card numbers, or a successful import.
- Missing optional dependencies or target hardware must produce an explicit skip, hold, abstention, or blocked state; do not fabricate a successful path.
- Every adaptive-routing digest reuses one code-owned `canonical_json_v1` implementation. It emits UTF-8 with no BOM/whitespace; preserves array order; sorts object keys by their UTF-8 byte sequence; escapes quote, backslash, and U+0000..U+001F deterministically (short escapes for backspace/tab/LF/form-feed/CR, otherwise lowercase `\u00xx`); leaves other valid Unicode as UTF-8 without global normalization; and rejects duplicate keys, invalid Unicode/surrogates, NaN/infinity, binary floats, and booleans where integers are required. Integers use minimal base-10 with zero exactly `0`; fractional measured values in digested records use schema-bounded canonical decimal strings with no exponent, leading plus/zeros, trailing fractional zeros, or negative zero. Null/true/false are lowercase. A record's own digest field is omitted entirely while referenced predecessor/child/schema/artifact digests remain; SHA-256 is over these exact bytes and encoded lowercase hex. Pretty JSON is never hashed. Every language/path reuses this implementation and known ASCII/Unicode/key-order/decimal/own-digest vectors; do not use implementation-native object formatting or cite an unimplemented canonicalization standard.
- Every fractional threshold, metric, latency, FPS display, coordinate, and ranking value uses one `CanonicalDecimalV1` string. Its exact full-match grammar is `\A-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]{0,17})(?:\.[0-9]{0,8}[1-9])?\z` (or the target language's equivalent fullmatch), at most 18 integer digits, 9 fractional digits, and 29 bytes including sign/dot. Exponent, plus, leading integer zero, trailing fractional zero, bare dot, over-scale, and over-length tokens are invalid. A token whose exact numeric value is zero is valid only as `0`; reject `-0`, while negative nonzero values such as `-0.1` remain available only where that field permits negatives. Each field schema further fixes sign and numeric range. Parse to an exact signed integer coefficient plus scale and compare/order/gate using checked arbitrary-precision integer scale alignment or an exact Decimal context with traps and no rounding. Never compare strings, convert to binary float, or use locale. Known vectors include valid `0`, `0.1`, `0.000000001`, `1.1`, and permitted `-0.1`; numeric 2 versus 10 and -2 versus -10; rejected equivalent/noncanonical spellings; 9-digit scale max/one-over; huge-token rejection; and exact just-at/over gates. Schemas, qualifier aggregation, selector ranking, reports, and decision traces reuse this implementation.
- Use authoritative units and names across every adaptive-routing schema. Request/report/decision latency and cold-start values are nonnegative CanonicalDecimalV1 milliseconds named `*_latency_ms` or `*_cold_start_ms`; do not store unlabeled p50/p95/p99 numbers. Monotonic measured intervals and elapsed durations are unsigned integer nanoseconds named `*_duration_ns`; memory and byte sizes are unsigned integers named `*_bytes`; counts are unsigned integers. Throughput/FPS gating is authoritative from an integer processed/sample count and integer duration_ns exact ratio; an optional CanonicalDecimalV1 display is rounded only for display by a fixed documented rule and is excluded from digests, comparisons, and gates. Unit-mismatch, second-versus-millisecond, float, overflow, display/gate divergence, and missing-unit fixtures must fail.
- Every persisted UTC instant uses exact RFC3339 UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`: four-digit year, valid Gregorian calendar date, two-digit fields, no offset, fractional second, leap second, or alternate spelling. Parse and compare instants rather than strings. Evidence validity is at most exactly `90 * 86400` seconds after report completion; monotonic duration_ns is separate and never derived by subtracting wall-clock strings. Reject invalid calendar dates, future timestamps where forbidden, overflow, offset/fraction/leap-second forms, reversed intervals, and one-second-over validity vectors.
- A `checksums.json` output is the checksum manifest, not a self-hashing file. It lists every other declared regular file with exact relative path, size, and SHA-256 plus the expected path set/count/total bytes; it never lists itself. Cover the manifest through the enclosing record/output digest when one exists, and test rejection of self-entry, missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, or mismatched entries.
- Any new CLI must support -h/--help. Any manifest change must keep tools/manifest.json and yolozu/data/manifest/tools_manifest.json synchronized.
acceptance_criteria: Versioned stream job/workload/result/qualification/selection interface contracts bind local MP4/camera parsing, queues, outputs, privacy, and soft-real-time evidence while rejecting RTSP/network/unqualified input.
notes:
2026-08-29 product gate: evidence-deferred. YOLOZU has no consented real streaming workload/SLO profile from YOLOZU-ll2.10 or YOLOZU-ll2.81.4.1, so MP4/camera semantics, queue policy, and measured targets cannot be grounded without guessing. Static-image P0 remains unchanged. Reopen when a consented non-personal workload profile fixes input, queue/drop, privacy, host, and SLO requirements.
2026-08-29 partial foundation merged in PR #287 (a377327): six canonical/packaged schemas and strict Python validators now cover StreamJobSpec, FrameResult, aggregate summary, unactivated qualification records, selection/abstention, source binding, and durable byte integrity. Contract, package, CI, and offline smoke checks passed. This is not closure evidence: no decoder or camera provider, live stream loop, queue/cancellation enforcement, slow-consumer real run, consented workload, real device, or measured 600-second/SLO evidence exists. Fixtures are not runtime or adoption evidence.

title: P2 add bounded streaming tracking and OCR lanes
description:
## Objective

After the bounded-image MVP is proven, add versioned streaming, tracking, and OCR interface contracts and Experimental local pipelines. These tasks do not expand the P0 promise and must not block the static-image foundation.

## Success Criteria

- Streaming has bounded queues, explicit drop semantics, cancellation/resource cleanup, and measured soft-real-time evidence; RTSP remains out of the first stream scope.
- Tracking output distinguishes detector observations from tracker predictions and excludes biometric identity or cross-stream identity linking.
- OCR output has a dedicated interface contract and never abuses detection class labels or leaks recognized text through telemetry/logs.
- Every adapter begins Candidate and reaches at most Experimental through exact evidence and the reviewed promotion workflow.

## Mandatory guardrails

- Keep the current Stable predictions validation and evaluation lane backward compatible. This program starts as Experimental.
- Natural-language interpretation belongs to the calling AI client. YOLOZU accepts typed data; do not embed an LLM in the core runtime.
- Candidate means metadata or an adapter exists; Candidate is never a default. Experimental requires qualification for an exact task and measured environment/workload fingerprint. Stable requires a separate reviewed promotion decision.
- Never treat unknown as zero, absent, passing, supported, or qualified. If required evidence or hardware is unavailable, record hold, skip, abstention, or blocked honestly.
- Do not download models, code, or datasets during recommendation or execution. Fetching is a separate explicit action with source, license, and SHA-256 checks.
- Do not upload images, prompts, filenames, host identifiers, raw event telemetry, or user datasets. Normal inference must complete without runner-requested network access after explicitly approved assets are present. P0 uses audited code-owned runners and is not an OS network sandbox; enforced isolation is separate P1 work.
- User-declared local output may contain workspace-relative input identifiers and mask paths required by the existing predictions interface contract. Those values remain in the local output and must not enter qualification evidence, selection decisions, telemetry, logs, or public summaries.
- Do not reopen the runtime-expansion decision YOLOZU-ll2.13. If a screened candidate needs a runtime/provider outside the existing shipped and qualified surfaces, screening must return hold and create a separate evidence-backed runtime decision/task covering demand, license, real inference, CI, and maintenance. An adapter task must not add that runtime silently.
- Keep TTA and TTT research in YOLOZU-ll2.54 separate. Research bundles are not selectable by this router.
- If a CLI or MCP surface changes, update implementation, tools/manifest.json, the packaged manifest, related docs/manual, generated references, and -h/--help behavior in the same change.
- Use the term interface contract for software interfaces. Run the repository-required manifest gates and focused tests named by the task; report unavailable hardware tests as unavailable rather than passing.
- Beads parent-child edges are organizational, not completion blockers. Never claim or close an epic merely because `bd ready` lists it. Before epic close, query all exact direct children, put their ID/title/status evidence table in the epic notes, and require every mandatory child closed. A conditional child may instead remain explicitly blocked or deferred only with its named current hold/reject/unavailable evidence and a concrete reconsideration trigger; an ordinary open/ready child never satisfies the audit. The root epic performs the same audit over all five direct child epics. If any condition is unmet, leave the epic open.
acceptance_criteria: Versioned streaming, tracking, and OCR interface contracts and bounded Experimental implementations are completed or evidence-deferred without changing the P0 static-image or Stable predictions boundaries.

title: P0 publish adaptive vision roadmap projection and drift gate
description:
## Objective

Publish the adaptive-vision roadmap as a claim-safe, machine-readable repository projection and keep its human-facing report, README links, packaged resource, and CI/CD checks synchronized. Beads remains the planning source of truth.

## Required changes

- Add one canonical packaged JSON projection for roadmap root `YOLOZU-ll2.81`, its five delivery epics, public scope, maturity target, and safety guardrails.
- Add a generated Markdown report under `reports/` and link it from the English README, Japanese README, docs index, roadmap, and production-readiness boundary.
- State that the router, model adapters, streaming, tracking, and OCR work are future Experimental delivery work; current Stable prediction validation/evaluation is unchanged.
- Add a deterministic generator/checker or equivalent bounded validator, focused tests, wheel/sdist coverage, and CI plus publish gates that fail on projection/report drift or a missing packaged resource.
- Keep any changed tool manifest and packaged copy byte-identical and update CLI help/docs if a generator CLI is added.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement routing, inference, algorithm adapters, qualification, promotion, streaming, tracking, or OCR.
- Do not call any candidate algorithm supported, qualified, selected, Stable, best, or latest.
- Do not duplicate live Beads task status into an independently authoritative tracker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- README.md and Readme_jp.md give a short, accurate roadmap entry and link to the generated report.
- The canonical JSON validates deterministically, is shipped in wheel and sdist, and identifies Beads as the planning source of truth.
- The tracked Markdown report is reproducible from the JSON and explicitly distinguishes current support from future target state.
- CI, pre-push, and publish workflows run the drift/package checks; focused and required manifest tests pass.
- All repository and Beads changes are committed and pushed; unrelated changes are preserved.

## Verification

Run the roadmap drift test/check, generator help when applicable, release-readiness docs tests, workflow tests, strict tool-manifest validation, packaged-manifest/docs-reference tests, packaging resource checks, and `git diff --check`.

## Execution guardrails

- Inspect existing SSOT, report-generation, package-data, and workflow conventions before editing.
- Use Beads as the planning source of truth and the JSON only as a dated public projection.
- Missing implementation or qualification evidence must remain explicit; never fabricate a capability or model result.
acceptance_criteria: A packaged machine-readable roadmap projection, generated report, README/docs links, and CI/CD drift gates agree without changing current support claims.
notes: Completed through PR #261 (https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/YOLOZU/pull/261), squash-merged to main as ea375722ff9fcb8e2be9a6c657ecc9e24aabcd13 on 2026-08-22. Published the claim-safe adaptive-vision projection, exact schema and packaged copies, deterministic tracked report, README/Readme_jp/docs links, tool manifests, generated CLI/web references, and pre-push/CI/publish/release drift and package gates. The projection cites beads-sync commit 9291cce8834c786f8d53aa181606131b958a0dcd and keeps Beads as the planning source of truth. Verification actually run: strict declarative manifest validation; focused roadmap, packaged-resource, docs-reference, readiness, workflow, release, SSOT, and web-doc suites; ruff; workflow YAML and shell syntax parsing; roadmap/web/integration reference drift checks; git diff checks; repeated pre-push gate including 48 focused tests, offline smoke, and real-image preflight; wheel and sdist build and archive inspection; installed-wheel importlib.resources readback outside the checkout. GitHub PR checks: 17 successful, 5 scope skips, 0 failures. Stable prediction validation/evaluation remains unchanged; adaptive routing, model adapters, streaming, tracking, and OCR are not implemented by this task and remain future Experimental work.

title: P1 decide third-party PyTorch candidate runtime surfaces
description:
## Objective

Decide whether the third-party PyTorch runtime surfaces required by the current
Grounding DINO plus SAM 2.1 and RF-DETR Nano 1.9.4 screenings may become shipped,
qualified YOLOZU adaptive runner/provider surfaces.

## Required evidence

Treat the two candidates separately. For each, record current legitimate product
demand, code and runtime license boundaries, immutable dependency and artifact
integrity, one real local inference path on a demanded host, maintainable CI and
release coverage, resource bounds, security review, and an explicit support and
maintenance owner or policy. Reuse the current hold screening records and do not
silently reopen YOLOZU-ll2.13.

## Boundary

Until this decision passes for a named candidate, its adapter and demanded-host
qualification Beads remain deferred. No package dependency, code, weight, model,
dataset, registry binding, support claim, or execution is authorized by creating
this task. Unavailable demand, hardware, artifact hashes, or license evidence stays
unknown or blocked rather than being backfilled.

## Verification

Use current official primary sources and real local evidence only. Any later code
change must run the repository-required manifest, package, focused, and CLI help
checks.
acceptance_criteria: Each named runtime surface has a separate evidence-backed pass or hold decision covering demand, license, real inference, CI, maintenance, resource, and security evidence before any adapter dependency or support claim.
notes:
Created from the 2026-08-29 Grounding DINO plus SAM 2.1 and RF-DETR Nano 1.9.4 hold screenings. Reconsider when a legitimate demanded host and complete immutable source/weight SHA-256 plus license evidence are available.
2026-08-29 completion evidence: PR #287 (merge a377327) records separate HOLD decisions for Grounding DINO plus SAM 2.1 and RF-DETR Nano 1.9.4 across demand, licenses, immutable integrity, real-local-inference availability, CI/release coverage, resources, security, and support/maintenance. No candidate dependency, code, model, weight, or dataset was downloaded or executed; unavailable evidence remains unknown. Reconsideration triggers are documented in docs/adaptive_runtime_surface_decisions_2026-08-29.md.
close_reason: Separate evidence-backed HOLD decisions merged in PR #287; neither runtime surface was approved or promoted.
